Turn 1 of 4 — read-back. Do not write any program JSON in this turn.

You are going to turn a workout into a Rhylthyme program: parallel **tracks** of sequential **steps**, each with a duration and a start trigger, that one person follows against a live clock.

Plan this as a Rhylthyme workout and deliver a live timeline: Partner Upper-Body Superset Session for 2 lifters
Resource limits: one bench and barbell, one pair of dumbbells, one pull-up bar, two ergs, about 25 minutes.
No finishing time was given; finish as early as the work allows.

Source text (read all of it):
<<<
Partner Upper-Body Superset Session

Two lifters, one flat bench with a barbell, one pair of dumbbells, one pull-up bar and two rowing ergs. The whole session should take about 25 minutes. You work as a pair: while Partner A is on the first exercise of a superset, Partner B is on the second, and then you swap; nobody waits for equipment if you keep the order.

Warm-up
Both partners start together with 5 minutes of easy rowing on the ergs, followed by 3 minutes of arm circles and band pull-aparts.

Superset A: bench press and dumbbell row (2 rounds)
Partner A loads the bar and does a set of 8 bench presses, which takes about 40 seconds. Partner B starts on the dumbbell row at the same time, 8 per side, also about 40 seconds. Then swap: A goes to the rows once B has finished with the dumbbells, and B takes the bench as soon as A racks the bar. After both exercises, rest 90 seconds before the next round. Do 2 rounds, resting after each.

Superset B: overhead press and pull-ups (2 rounds)
Move straight on after the last rest. Partner A does 8 strict overhead presses with the dumbbells, about 45 seconds, while Partner B does a set of pull-ups, 6 to 10 reps, about 30 seconds. Swap when both are done: A moves to the pull-up bar, and B takes the dumbbells when A sets them down. Rest 2 minutes between rounds; there is no rest after the second round.

Cool-down
Finish together with 5 minutes of stretching: doorway chest stretch, lat stretch on the pull-up bar, and slow shoulder rolls.
>>>

Read all of it before you answer. Then say back, in one paragraph and in your own words: what is being made, for how many (or at what scale), by when, and under what constraints — equipment that exists only once, how many people are working, anything that has to be held, rested or ready at a particular moment. If the text you were given looks truncated, or points at a section that is not here, say so instead of filling the gap.

End your reply with the same read-back as JSON in a single ```json fenced block:

```json
{
  "summary": "one paragraph: what is being made, for how many, by when, under what constraints",
  "servesOrScale": "8 people",
  "deadline": "2026-11-26T18:00:00",
  "constraints": ["one oven", "two burners", "two cooks"]
}
```

The task is to create a Rhylthyme program for a Partner Upper-Body Superset Session workout, designed for 2 lifters working together. The session should be completed in about 25 minutes, with no specific finishing time given, so the goal is to finish as early as the work allows. The constraints include having only one bench and barbell, one pair of dumbbells, one pull-up bar, and two rowing ergs available. The workout involves a warm-up, two supersets (A and B), and a cool-down, with specific exercises and rest periods in between.

```json
{
  "summary": "A Partner Upper-Body Superset Session workout for 2 lifters, to be completed in about 25 minutes, with constraints on equipment availability.",
  "servesOrScale": "2 lifters",
  "deadline": "as soon as possible",
  "constraints": ["one bench and barbell", "one pair of dumbbells", "one pull-up bar", "two rowing ergs"]
}
```

Here's the restatement of the target data model in my own words:

- A **track** represents a sequential workflow where steps do not overlap; parallel work is represented across different tracks.
- A **step** has a single duration type: `fixed`, `variable`, or `indefinite`, with corresponding parameters.
- A **startTrigger** determines when a step begins, referencing either the program start time, another step, or a manual trigger.
- `stepId`s must be unique across the entire program.
- Every `task` used by a step requires a corresponding `resourceConstraints` entry, which defines the maximum number of concurrent users for that task.
- Repeated work is modeled using `replicates` on a single step, with options to chain subsequent steps per instance or wait for all instances to complete.

For the Partner Upper-Body Superset Session workout, the expected resource constraints are:

- `erg`: 2 (two rowing ergs available)
- `bench_and_barbell`: 1 (one bench and barbell available)
- `dumbbells`: 1 (one pair of dumbbells available)
- `pull_up_bar`: 1 (one pull-up bar available)

There are 2 actors (lifters) working together.

```json
{
  "acknowledgement": "tracks are sequential lines of work; one duration kind per step; triggers link steps; every task needs a resourceConstraint; stepIds are global",
  "resourceConstraints": [
    { "task": "erg", "maxConcurrent": 2 },
    { "task": "bench_and_barbell", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "dumbbells", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "pull_up_bar", "maxConcurrent": 1 }
  ],
  "actors": 2
}
```

Partner A loads the bar and does a set of 8 bench presses, which takes about 40 seconds. Partner B starts on the dumbbell row at the same time, 8 per side, also about 40 seconds. Then swap: A goes to the rows once B has finished with the dumbbells, and B takes the bench as soon as A racks the bar. After both exercises, rest 90 seconds before the next round. Do 2 rounds, resting after each.

Move straight on after the last rest. Partner A does 8 strict overhead presses with the dumbbells, about 45 seconds, while Partner B does a set of pull-ups, 6 to 10 reps, about 30 seconds. List every timed activity you would have to perform, in the order the text gives it, with:

- a short kebab-case `stepId` and a human `name`;
- `task`: the resource it occupies while it runs — the oven, a burner, the thermocycler, the PA, the bench, your own hands. Use the same name every time for the same resource;

- `sourceSpan`: the exact words in the text you took it from, as `{"quote": "...", "occurrence": n}`, where n says which occurrence of those words you mean (1 for the first). Quote the text verbatim — do not paraphrase it;
- `inferred`: `true` for a step the text never states but the work needs anyway (preheating, thawing, resting, cooling, labelling, sound-check), with `"sourceSpan": null`. Keep these few and obvious.

Split anything the text bundles into one sentence when the parts occupy different resources or different stretches of time ("brown the meat, then simmer for 40 minutes" is two activities). Do not decide yet which activities can overlap, which track they belong to, or what waits for what.
